'''Guillaume Carlier''' is a French [[mathematician]]. Most of his work lies in the field of [[calculus of variation]] and [[optimization]]. He is a [[professor]] of [[applied mathematics]] at [[Paris Dauphine University]] and a researcher at Mokaplan, a joint [[INRIA]]-[[CNRS]]-Université Paris-Dauphine team dedicated to research in the field of [[optimal transport]].<ref name="Ceremade">{{cite web |last1=Carlier |first1=Guillaume |title=CVtheque |url=https://dauphine.psl.eu/recherche/cvtheque/carlier-guillaume |website=Université Paris Dauphine |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref><ref name="Mokaplan">{{cite web |last1=INRIA |title=Team members |url=https://team.inria.fr/mokaplan/team-members/ |website=Mokaplan |date=21 July 2011 |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

==Life and work==
Carlier's work mainly focuses on applied mathematics, in particular in the fields of [[calculus of variations]], [[optimization]], [[convex analysis]], and [[optimal transport|transportation theory]] as well as their application to [[economics]] and traffic modelling.<ref name="Ceremade" /><ref name="TUM">{{cite web |last1=Carlier |first1=Guillaume |title=Fakultät Mathematik Lehrstuhl für Höhere Mathematik und Analytische Mechanik |url=http://www-m8scheurle.ma.tum.de/m8/gaeste/carlier/ |website=Technische Universität München |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref><ref name="SpringerProfile">{{cite web |title=Guillaume Carlier |url=https://link.springer.com/search?dc.creator=%22Guillaume+Carlier%22 |website=Authors profiles |publisher=Springer |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

He graduated in mathematics and mathematical economics from [[ENSAE ParisTech]], [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], and Paris-Dauphine University in 1996. He then completed his PhD at Paris-Dauphine University in 2000, with a dissertation on the applications of calculus of variations to contract theory, under the supervision of [[Ivar Ekeland]].<ref name="theses">{{cite web |title=Guillaume Carlier |url=https://www.theses.fr/110771044 |website=theses.fr |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref> After his studies, he was an assistant professor at the [[University of Bordeaux]] and then moved to Paris-Dauphine University, where he is now a professor.<ref name="Ceremade" /> He is a member of Mokaplan,<ref name="Mokaplan" /> a joint research unit co-sponsored by Paris-Dauphine University, the [[National Centre for Scientific Research]], and the [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation]].<ref name="Inria">{{cite web |title=Mokaplan |url=https://team.inria.fr/mokaplan/ |website=Inria |date=21 July 2011 |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>
